name: Koderma–Balasore Highway
aka: Formed from the former NH 32, and parts of NH 33 and NH 5 (old numbering)
history: NH 18 is the highway of India's coal and steel country. From Koderma in Jharkhand it passes Giridih, the coal capital Dhanbad, the steel cities of Bokaro and Jamshedpur, and the hills of Purulia in West Bengal, before dropping down through Baripada to Balasore near the Odisha coast. Most of it was made up of the old NH 32, NH 33 and NH 5 before the highways were renumbered.
facts: Serves India's coal and steel heartland: Dhanbad, Bokaro and Jamshedpur all lie on it.
Made from the old NH 32 plus parts of the old NH 33 and NH 5.
Crosses from Jharkhand into West Bengal's Purulia district and back into Jharkhand before ending in Odisha.
Ends near Balasore, close to Chandipur beach, where the sea goes out several kilometres at low tide.
